overall: Independence Day in Los Angeles is expected to be mostly cloudy with onshore flow keeping temperatures mild, with a high near 70°F. Southwest winds of 0–10 mph will dominate, and there are active air quality alerts for fine particle and ozone pollution, though no severe weather is anticipated. Conditions are typical of a June Gloom-adjacent marine influence pattern extending into early July.
forecast_obs_notes: Model agreement is moderate with a slight warm bias in the forecast-only models versus the observation-weighted ensemble. ECMWF, GFS, HRRR, and NBM all favor 72–73°F as their top bucket with expected values clustering 70.6–72.0°F, while GEM and WEATHER_COM lean cooler at 69.9°F and 69.4°F respectively, suggesting some spread on whether marine influence suppresses the afternoon high below 70°F.
max_temp_prediction: The ensemble expected TMAX of 70.5°F is the best anchor, modestly pulled down from the forecast-only 73.0°F by cooler prior-day observations (yesterday's high was only 64.9°F). The odd bucket set's top bucket of 71–72°F at 42.5% probability (Tier 1, high confidence) and the even bucket set's top of 72–73°F at 38.0% together point to a most likely range of 70–73°F, with the 71–72°F range having the strongest single-bucket support. Confidence is moderately high given Tier 1 signals in both bucket sets, but the cooler recent obs introduce modest downside risk toward the 68–70°F range.
